chapter: Trumpet teachers and St. Louis heroes
title: Sobbing Blues and hearing Louis Armstrong's sound
summary: Studying Louis Armstrong, Thomas recalls going next door to hear Bessie Smith's Sobbing Blues and other records on Uncle Floyd's Saturday record sessions.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: Now, this might be interesting to you. During that time, must be around ... maybe I did but we had a lot of things to talk about. During that time I'm studying, too. I mean the great Louis Armstrong. Please don't misunderstand me because he knew how I felt about him. Oh, there came a time during that time, Bessie had recorded a blues, called it Sobbing Blues.
Sobbing Blues, around that time and I'd go to my Uncle Floyd to hear it. So I hope this gives you ... because it always does me. So, St. Louis ...
Your uncle was in St. Louis?
Next door, remember? Webster Groves, right?
No, no. I mean the incident I'm talking -- the musical incident would have to be St. Louis.
Yeah. But, I mean is your uncle in St. Louis?

No, he's next door. And I go and listen to records on Saturday. Tremendous person. And he'd have his records on and he'd been out shopping. And, he'd bring these things in. He had them there, really, and I'd go visiting. And, Joe Smith Henderson had played something and the-emphasis had been on some of these records, too, with Mamie Amy Smith, and Joe Smith had been on some of these records. But, Louis Armstrong, I heard his instrument.
I heard his sound and his instrument. So I found out who he was. ...
